 Advertisement Updated: 8:50 AM CST Nov 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jonathan Greco Digital Media Manager INTERACTIVE MAP: Tracking early voting data in Oklahoma
 Updated: 8:50 AM CST Nov 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jonathan Greco Digital Media Manager Early voting is officially underway in Oklahoma as people will decide on numerous key statewide and federal races on the ballot. 
 IMPORTANT ELECTION INFORMATION: Finding Your Polling Place | Finding Your Sample Ballot | Absentee Ballot Voting | Early Voting | Full List of Races | Meet Candidates Across the State | Who is Mike Mazzei? | Who is Cyndi Munson? 
 Advertisement Oklahomans will vote on the gubernatorial race, lieutenant governor race, all five Congressional District seats, two state questions, state superintendent race, and more. 
 The Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early and mail-in ballots nationwide ahead of Election Day, Nov. 3. The data comes from the University of Florida Election Lab . 
 Use the map above to see how many early votes have been cast in each state, including mail-in ballots accepted and early votes. 
 In 31 states plus Washington, D.C., voters can register under a party affiliation. When that data is available, it is included under a state's data. Not all states allow or have opened early voting yet.
 When is early voting in Oklahoma?
 Oklahoma has four days right before the election set aside for early voting. The dates for early voting are:
 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Oct. 28 
 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Oct. 29 
 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Oct. 30 
 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. Oct. 31 
 This content is imported from infogram. You may be able to find the same content in another format, or you may be able to find more information, at their web site. Where can you participate in early voting?
 To participate in early voting, you'll need to go to your county election board or a designated early voting location.
 You can find a list of early voting locations here .
 What do I need to vote?
 Oklahoma law requires every voter who casts their ballot in person to show proof of identity before receiving a ballot. Below are the three ways to show proof of identity.
 Show a valid photo ID issued by the federal, state or tribal government.
 Show the free voter identification card issued to every voter by their county election board.
 Sign an affidavit and vote a provisional ballot. (If the information on the affidavit matches official voter registration records, the ballot will be counted after Election Day.)
 If you have any one of those three, you'll be allowed to cast your ballot in Oklahoma's general election.
